A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TIGeR research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E are readable and support reliable comparison despite renaming and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, retrieval, ablation, and prompt-extension results on TIGeR-Bench, Flickr30K, and MS-COCO, including extensive experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds agent comparisons, VisDial results, and domain-specific retrieval-selection statistics.

M1.justification: Sections 3 and Appendix B retain the same discrete tokenization, Trie-constrained beam search, reverse reranking, synchronous generation/retrieval, and likelihood-based decision procedure. Naming the framework TIGeR-ONE, labeling the debiasing score as PMI, and explaining beam search do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v2 adds VisDial for dialogue-conditioned image acquisition in Section 5.2 and Table 4. This extends existing dialogue coverage: v1 already evaluated synthetic TIGeR-Bench chat scenarios and multimodal interactions. The original datasets and eight TIGeR-Bench domains remain.

E2.justification: Table 2 substantially strengthens the unified comparison beyond GILL by adding SDXL + CLIP agents using SEED-LLaMA or Qwen2-VL for decisions. The new VisDial comparison includes GLIDE and SD-v1.5, and Figure 5 adds GILL to the efficiency comparison. The original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The VisDial experiment introduces CLIP-I evaluation after 1, 5, and 10 dialogue rounds. Figure 5 changes the reported database-size sweep to points spanning 10^8–10^11. Existing benchmark construction, main accuracy metrics, and Appendix C.2 implementation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 Table 10 adds domain-specific retrieval-selection percentages, extending v1's aggregate percentages and qualitative observations about decision behavior. Figure 5 expands the existing efficiency analysis. The original reranking, decision, debiasing, beam-size, prompt-extension, and qualitative analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results follow the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Matched existing numerical tables retain their values, including v1 Table 10 relocated as v2 Table 6. Substantial new results include the Qwen2-VL agent's 27.91/60.65 CLIP-T/CLIP-I scores, VisDial results such as unified SEED-LLaMA scoring 70.9 versus generation-only 67.9 after 10 rounds, and domain-specific selection rates. Figure 5 also replaces throughput curves under a changed size sweep; this does not establish a same-setting speed improvement.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the forward-pass complexity argument are retained. Added argmax notation, PMI terminology, and standard beam-search exposition restate existing scoring and search concepts; no substantive new theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation appears.

C1.justification: Both versions claim training-free unification of generation and retrieval, intrinsic likelihood-based discrimination, autonomous image selection, and the TIGeR-Bench contribution. The single-LMM and model-agnostic emphasis in v2 clarifies properties already present in v1 without materially changing the central scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 replaces v1's caution that generated/retrieved differences may demand stronger discrimination with an argument that reusing computed similarities makes decisions incur no additional computational cost. Section 5.4 adds interpretations about identity preservation and maintaining retrieved characteristics during interactions. Existing decision-error examples and future-work limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that code, models, and the benchmark are available at the existing project site, and identifies the new agent components and backbones. Conversely, relocating v1 Table 10 to v2 Table 6 omits its explicit SEED-LLaMA-only and 200-beam caption details. The main implementation settings in Appendix C.2 are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges knowledge-intensive generation work through Re-Imagen and KITTEN, expands the discussion of GILL's alignment costs, and connects debiasing to PMI literature. It adds references for the new evaluations and beam-search background while removing some references, including the WIT dataset paper. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: The title, framework name, and MLLM/LMM terminology change, with prose revisions across the abstract, introduction, and methodology. Proxy explanations gain explicit headings, Appendix B gains a beam-search subsection, and chat-expansion discussion moves into the main text. The overall section sequence and most appendix prose are retained.

P2.justification: The presentation is substantially revised through ICLR formatting, redrawn Figures 1 and 7, restyled Figures 2 and 6, and new axes and legends in Figure 5. Table 2 gains agent rows, new VisDial and selection-rate tables appear, and the earlier appendix chat table becomes a compact main-text table. Most appendix qualitative examples remain the same.

improvement.justification: The expert-agent baselines address v1's limited unified comparison, while VisDial adds quantitative support for dialogue applications beyond the existing synthetic chats and examples. Domain-specific selection rates and clearer proxy explanations also help interpretation. These gains are limited by sparse reproducibility details for the new evaluations and the loss of explicit model and beam settings from the relocated chat table.
